Hinojosa Lets Data Centers Finish, But There Is a Catch
Texas's First Democrat Governor in 36 Years Turns to SpaceX
Why Hinojosa's SpaceX Pause Matters More Than Her Win

descs.t: Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says every data center already permitted in Texas will be allowed to finish construction. She also asked for a pause on land talks with SpaceX in her first news conference since the win. We walk through what she said and what it means for tech in Texas.

Gina Hinojosa, the first Democrat to win the Texas governor's race in 36 years, says data centers can finish but the state's deal with business has to change into a partnership. Her first move was a pause on land talks with SpaceX. We look at what that means for Elon Musk, for jobs and for the voters who flipped the state.

Blue Texas has its first test, and it is Elon Musk's land deal. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa paused SpaceX land talks and set new terms for data centers: they can finish, but from now on it has to be a partnership. We break down who wins, who pays and what happens next.

intro.plain: Texas has a Democrat governor-elect for the first time in 36 years, and Gina Hinojosa is already setting terms. She says every data center already permitted can finish construction, and she asked for a pause on land talks with SpaceX. So the question for the chat: is a pause on SpaceX a smart start or a bad signal to business?
intro.mid: Gina Hinojosa won Texas and her first big move is about tech, not the border. Data centers already permitted can finish, she says, but from now on it has to be a partnership that benefits Texans. And she paused land talks with SpaceX. Chat, tell me: is that a fair deal or a shakedown of business?
intro.bold: Texas went blue, and the first company to feel it is SpaceX. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa paused land talks with Elon Musk's company and put new terms on data centers: finish what is permitted, then a partnership that benefits Texans. Chat, who blinks first: Hinojosa or Musk?

hook.plain: The first Democrat to win the Texas governor's race in 36 years just paused land talks with SpaceX. Here is what she said about data centers, and what changes for tech in Texas.
hook.mid: Hinojosa says data centers can finish, then adds a condition. That condition, and her pause on SpaceX, tells you how blue Texas plans to deal with Big Tech.
hook.bold: Blue Texas picked its first fight, and it is with Elon Musk. Here is the SpaceX pause, the new data center terms, and what it means for every tech company in Texas.

descs.t: Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's US Senate race by about 2,500 votes, with 97% of the expected vote counted and the race still uncalled. We go through the latest ballot drops and what is still left to count.

Mississippi's Senate race is still being counted two days on, and Cindy Hyde-Smith has fallen further behind Scott Colom with each batch. Both parties are preparing for a legal fight. We look at where the votes are coming from and what could still change.

A Democrat is ahead in a Mississippi Senate race, and if the lead holds, Scott Colom would be the state's first Democratic senator elected since 1982, according to the betting markets. We walk through the count, the lawyers and what it means for control of the Senate.

intro.plain: Mississippi is still counting. Democrat Scott Colom now leads Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,500 votes, with 97% of the expected vote in, and his lead has grown with almost every batch. Both parties are getting ready for a legal fight. So tell me in the chat: should a count this close go to a recount?
intro.mid: Two days after the vote, Mississippi still has no winner in its Senate race, and Cindy Hyde-Smith keeps slipping. Scott Colom is ahead by about 2,500 votes and the lawyers are already moving in on both sides. This is a seat Republicans never expected to sweat. Chat, what went wrong for Hyde-Smith?
intro.bold: A Democrat is winning a Senate race in Mississippi. Scott Colom is up about 2,500 votes on Cindy Hyde-Smith with almost everything counted, and the markets now give him around 98 to 99 percent. If it holds, it is the state's first Democratic senator since 1982. Chat, is this a warning shot for Republicans or a one off?

hook.plain: Scott Colom leads Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,500 votes in Mississippi, and the race is still uncalled. Here is where the last votes are coming from.
hook.mid: Two days of counting and Cindy Hyde-Smith keeps falling behind. Here is why Mississippi's Senate race is headed for the lawyers.
hook.bold: Mississippi could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time since 1982. Here is how close it is, and who is getting ready to fight it.

Trump Just Made His Gold Oval Office Untouchable
Oval Office and Cabinet Room Are Now Monuments. Who Can Undo It?
Trump Uses the Antiquities Act on His Own Office
Why Trump Wants the Next President Unable to Redecorate
Trump to Every Future President: Hands OFF My Oval Office

descs.t: President Trump signed a proclamation making the Oval Office a national monument under the Antiquities Act. Posts from his own staff say the Cabinet Room is covered too, and that both rooms are meant to stay as they are. Here is what the proclamation says and what it can and cannot stop.

Trump has used the Antiquities Act on the Oval Office itself, declaring it a national monument. Supporters call it protecting a historic room; critics say it ties the hands of the next president. Here is what the proclamation covers and how hard it would be to reverse.

Trump says the Oval Office will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, and he signed a proclamation making it a national monument to make that stick. The next president walks into a room he may not be able to change. Here is what that means for every president who comes after him.

intro.plain: President Trump has signed a proclamation making the Oval Office a national monument under the Antiquities Act, and posts from his staff say the Cabinet Room is included. He says it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody. So here is my question for the chat: should one president be able to decide what the next one's office looks like?
intro.mid: Trump just used the Antiquities Act on his own office. The Oval Office, and by several accounts the Cabinet Room, are now national monuments, and he says nobody will be allowed to touch them. Tell me in the chat: is this protecting history, or locking in one president's taste for good?
intro.bold: Trump has made the Oval Office a national monument. His words: it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody. The next president walks into a room he may not be able to change. Chat, be honest: would you undo it on day one, or leave it alone?

hook.plain: The Oval Office is now a national monument. Trump signed the proclamation himself. Here is what it covers and whether a future president could undo it.
hook.mid: Trump just used the Antiquities Act on his own office. Here is what that proclamation really locks in, and whether it lasts.
hook.bold: Trump says nobody will ever be allowed to touch the Oval Office again. He signed a monument order to make it stick. Can it actually stop the next president?

descs.t: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed explains why he will not back Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader and supports Chris Van Hollen instead. He is not alone: Annie Andrews, Troy Jackson and Peggy Flanagan say the same. We walk through who has said no and what it means for the vote.

Chuck Schumer spent $30M to help elect Abdul El-Sayed, and now El-Sayed wants him out of Senate leadership. Several new Democratic senators are calling for generational change while Trump says Schumer probably gets the job. We look at the count and the case for Chris Van Hollen.

Chuck Schumer just won the Senate and his own new senators are lining up against him. Abdul El-Sayed, Annie Andrews, Troy Jackson and Peggy Flanagan all say no, and Trump calls Schumer not a bad guy. We break down whether the revolt can actually remove him.

intro.plain: Chuck Schumer has a problem inside his own party. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed says he will not back Schumer for majority leader and supports Chris Van Hollen. Annie Andrews, Troy Jackson and Peggy Flanagan say the same. Chat, does Schumer keep his job, yes or no?
intro.mid: Schumer reportedly spent $30M to help elect Abdul El-Sayed, and now El-Sayed wants him out of leadership. New senators are calling for generational change, while Trump says Schumer probably gets it and is not a bad guy. Chat, does a Trump compliment help or hurt Schumer right now?
intro.bold: Chuck Schumer just won the Senate, and his own new senators are turning on him. El-Sayed, Andrews, Jackson, Flanagan: all say no. Van Hollen says he won't back anyone who won't take on big fights. Chat, is Schumer finished as leader?

hook.plain: Abdul El-Sayed says he will not vote for Chuck Schumer as majority leader. Here is why, and the other new senators who agree.
hook.mid: Schumer spent $30M to elect him. Now El-Sayed wants Schumer gone. Here is the fight for Senate leadership and who could replace him.
hook.bold: Chuck Schumer's new majority is revolting before it is even sworn in. Here is every senator saying no, and whether they can actually take him down.

descs.t: Reports from Bloomberg and The Independent say Secretary of State Marco Rubio is considering resigning after the midterms to launch a 2028 presidential bid. The State Department says he is not resigning. We walk through what each side says and what we actually know.

Marco Rubio is reportedly discussing resignation with White House officials, yet he was back at the White House for meetings and the State Department says he is staying. We look at his split with JD Vance over the war and what a 2028 run would mean for him.

Marco Rubio is defending the war while JD Vance walks away from it, and now reports say Rubio may quit to run in 2028. The State Department says he is going nowhere. We break down why his staying or leaving matters for the pressure on the Islamic Republic.

intro.plain: Is Marco Rubio leaving? Bloomberg and The Independent report he is considering resigning as Secretary of State to run for president in 2028. The State Department says he is not resigning, and he was at the White House today for meetings. Chat, what do you think: does Rubio stay or go?
intro.mid: Rubio is reportedly talking resignation with the White House, but the State Department says he is staying. Reports also say he split with JD Vance and is still defending the war. Chat, is Rubio the 2028 frontrunner if he leaves?
intro.bold: While JD Vance backs away from the war with the Islamic Republic, Marco Rubio is defending it. Now reports say Rubio could quit to run in 2028, and the State Department flatly denies it. If he goes, the regime loses one of its toughest opponents in Washington. Chat, should Rubio stay?

hook.plain: Reports say Marco Rubio may resign to run in 2028. The State Department says no. Here is what each side says and what we know for sure.
hook.mid: The same day reports said Rubio was quitting, the State Department said he is going nowhere. Here is what is really going on with the Secretary of State.
hook.bold: Rubio is standing by the war with the Islamic Republic as Vance walks away, and now resignation rumors swirl. Here is why it matters who runs American foreign policy.
